stances.claim: The Javellana 6-4 vote can and should be rendered as the roster of names in the dispositive, not in abstract: Makalintal, Castro, Barredo, Makasiar, Antonio, and Esguerra for the majority against Concepcion (CJ), Zaldivar, Fernando, and Teehankee -- a transparency of roster that lets each reader weigh history's verdict.
stances.rhetorical_move: primary-text fidelity (quoting the dispositive verbatim instead of paraphrasing)

stances.claim: The Marcos LNMB interment was justified by the Ocampo majority on four procedural-doctrinal grounds (political question, no locus standi, non-exhaustion of administrative remedies, non-observance of the hierarchy of courts) plus a substantive finding that the order did not contravene constitutional, local, or international human rights law and was not whimsical/capricious/arbitrary.

The Lambino MR was denied with finality on Nov 21, 2006 by the same 8-7 vote -- the roster bears recording: Carpio as ponente, joined by CJ Panganiban himself, Santiago, Gutierrez, Austria-Martinez, Carpio Morales, Callejo, Azcuna; against the dissent of Puno joined by Quisumbing, Corona, Tinga, Chico-Nazario, Garcia, Velasco -- making the 8-7 doctrinal alignment a matter of historical record.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-disclosure of own concurring vote within the roster

stances.claim: On party-list abolition -- Duterte's wish, Sotto's empowerment-of-Comelec bill, and Macalintal's reverse-the-decisions suggestion remain unprogressed; CJ's response to Macalintal was that he, as a seasoned election lawyer, could himself initiate the solution.

On Sereno reinstatement: to CJ's knowledge no petition has been filed; former Ombudsman Carpio Morales texted that Sereno should be considered a 'de facto Justice to be granted the same benefits given to Corona' -- a framing that, if adopted, would address the benefits question without forcing the reinstatement issue.

On why only five cases -- sufficient column space, not lack of game-changing material -- Marcelo's coco-levy reminder (CJ's own December 2001 ponencia declaring the coco levy funds prima facie public funds; ~P70B collected and placed in trust; small coconut farmers still not benefiting to this day), Davide's Estrada constructive-resignation inquiry, and other friends' pork-barrel references all merit future columns.
stances.confidence: asserted with self-disclosure of own coco-levy ponencia

notable_anecdotes: The Javellana roster recitation -- including, in CJ Concepcion's own dispositive language, 'This being the vote of the majority, there is no further judicial obstacle to the new Constitution being considered in force and effect' -- used to anchor the reader directly to the primary text rather than to summary.

Lambino MR same-vote 8-7 finality -- and CJ's self-disclosure that he himself was one of the eight concurring with Carpio's ponencia -- a quiet moment of historical-record honesty within a Q&A column.

Conchita Carpio Morales texting CJ that Sereno should be considered a 'de facto Justice to be granted the same benefits given to Corona' -- the most quotable third-party framing of the Sereno-benefits question, offered as a text from a retired Ombudsman.

Simeon Marcelo's email reminding CJ that the December 2001 coco-levy decision (declaring the funds prima facie public, ~P70B eventually collected into trust) was CJ's own ponencia -- 'the first legal victory for the poorest of the poor small coconut farmers' -- and that 'to this day, the protracted war continues.'
Davide's inquiry on the Estrada 'constructive resignation' ouster -- the canonical case of presidential-removal-without-impeachment -- flagged for future column.
Closing 'thank you, readers' acknowledgment plus the promise to answer 'directly or indirectly' in future columns -- the canonical Q&A closing template.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban responds to reader questions on his previous Sunday's 'Five game-changing SC decisions' column. Q1 -- the Javellana v. Executive Secretary 6-4 majority comprised Makalintal, Castro, Barredo, Makasiar, Antonio, and Esguerra against the dissent of CJ Concepcion (the ponente), Zaldivar, Fernando, and Teehankee, with Concepcion's dispositive: 'there is no further judicial obstacle to the new Constitution being considered in force and effect.' Q2 -- Ocampo v. Enriquez's allowance of the Marcos LNMB interment was based on the Peralta ponencia's four grounds (political question, no locus standi, failure to exhaust administrative remedies, non-observance of the hierarchy of courts) plus a substantive finding of no constitutional/local/international-human-rights contravention; concurring were JJ Velasco, Leonardo-De Castro, Brion, Bersamin, Del Castillo, Perez, Mendoza, Perlas-Bernabe; dissenting were CJ Sereno and JJ Carpio, Leonen, Jardeleza, Caguioa, with J Reyes no part. Q3 -- the Lambino MR was denied with finality on Nov 21, 2006 by the same 8-7 vote, with Carpio as ponente joined by Panganiban himself, Santiago, Gutierrez, Austria-Martinez, Carpio Morales, Callejo, and Azcuna, against the dissent of Puno joined by Quisumbing, Corona, Tinga, Chico-Nazario, Garcia, and Velasco. Q4 -- on party-list abolition, Duterte's wish and Sotto's bill (empowering Comelec to refuse or cancel a party-list's registration) remain unprogressed; Macalintal's reverse-the-decisions proposal was returned by CJ to Macalintal himself ('as a seasoned election lawyer, could initiate the solution'). Q5 -- to CJ's knowledge no petition has been filed to reinstate Sereno or grant her retirement benefits, but former Ombudsman Conchita Carpio Morales texted that Sereno should be considered a 'de facto Justice to be granted the same benefits given to Corona.' Q6 -- many readers asked why only five cases: Simeon Marcelo emailed at length on the December 2001 coco-levy public-funds decision (of which CJ was the ponente; ~P70 billion eventually collected into trust, yet small coconut farmers still not benefiting); retired CJ Hilario G. Davide Jr. inquired about Estrada's constructive-resignation ouster; others asked about the pork-barrel rulings. CJ's short answer: insufficient space to cover them all in one column. 'But, thank you, readers for your questions. In the future, I hope to answer them, directly or indirectly.'
